findings.title: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool
findings.body: The strategy is constructed with the FixedQueuePool that ResultsStrategyFactory creates once and reuses. close() ultimately calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(), permanently stopping the worker threads and queues. Arroyo can create a new processing strategy after rebalances using the same factory, so any later strategy would be backed by a dead pool and would not process messages. Strategy close should only stop its own commit thread, or the factory must create/reset a pool per strategy.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit() calls put() without blocking or rejecting. If a group assigned to a queue is slow, the consumer continues polling and enqueueing work indefinitely. This can grow memory and offset-tracking state without bound and potentially OOM the consumer, despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked completed and can be committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches Exception from the result processor and then unconditionally marks the offset complete in finally. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows handle_result exceptions. A message that fails processing is therefore treated as done and can be committed by the background commit loop, permanently skipping it. This contradicts the stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing; failures need retry, DLQ, or explicit drop handling.

findings.title: Submission errors silently drop messages and mark offsets complete
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions from decoding, grouping, or enqueueing and, when the message has broker metadata, adds the offset and immediately completes it. A malformed payload or a bug in grouping_fn can therefore cause the message to be skipped while its offset becomes committable. There is no DLQ, retry, or failure metric to make this data loss visible.

findings.title: close() stops the commit loop before draining the queue pool
findings.body: close() sets the shutdown event, joins the commit thread, and only then shuts down the FixedQueuePool. If queue_pool.shutdown() processes any remaining queued items, those items complete after the last commit opportunity, so their offsets will not be committed and they will be reprocessed after restart. The shutdown order should allow draining and then perform a final commit, or commit while draining.

findings.title: OffsetTracker state persists across partition assignments
findings.body: OffsetTracker is owned by the long-lived FixedQueuePool and is never reset or pruned when partitions are revoked or reassigned. Outstanding offsets from a revoked partition can remain forever. If the same partition is later reassigned with different offsets, a stale outstanding offset can create an artificial gap that blocks get_committable_offsets() from committing newer offsets, and old partition state leaks.

findings.title: Committable-offset calculation scans potentially huge offset ranges
findings.body: get_committable_offsets() iterates over every integer offset from the first possible uncommitted offset through max(all_offsets). If one old offset remains outstanding because of a slow worker, shutdown loss, or stale tracker state, this scan is repeated every commit cycle and can become very expensive for large offset ranges, while also hiding the fact that one offset is stuck.

findings.title: max_workers is not validated for positive values
findings.body: In thread-queue-parallel mode the pool is created with num_queues=max_workers or 20. Passing --max-workers 0 silently becomes 20, and passing a negative value creates a pool with no queues, leading to IndexError or modulo issues when submitting work. The CLI option or factory should validate that max_workers is greater than zero.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts behavior the implementation does not guarantee
findings.body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling makes the result processor raise for one message and asserts that no offset is committed. However the worker catches the exception and marks the offset complete, so the background commit loop can commit it if it runs before the test shuts everything down. The test currently depends on shutting down before the commit timer fires, making it flaky and validating the wrong contract.

findings.title: WorkItem retains the full Kafka message unnecessarily
findings.body: WorkItem stores the original Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], but workers only use partition, offset, and result. Keeping the full Kafka payload in queues increases memory usage, which is especially problematic because the queues are unbounded. The message field can be removed or replaced with only the needed metadata.
